title: Asynchronous model fanout and incremental refresh reference
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview

This document defines a reference architecture and operational playbook for deploying Redwood inference model artifacts to private (VPC or on-prem) edge sites where connectivity is constrained or intermittent. The strategy is an asynchronous model fanout with signed manifests and incremental (delta) refreshes so that local runtime instances can serve requests with predictable latency while minimizing bandwidth and preserving auditability.

Scope

- Applies to private deployments that operate in low-bandwidth, high-latency, or scheduled-connectivity environments (examples: retail kiosks, branch offices, manufacturing sites, regulated air-gapped facilities with nightly sync windows).
- Covers control-plane manifests, artifact packaging, delta computation, local runtime behavior, rollout/upgrade procedures, and day-2 operational checks.
- Does not replace normal hot-swap model-rollout flows used by always-on data center deployments; this is a specialization for constrained environments.

Goals and design constraints

1. Serve local inference requests with P95 tail latency <= 300ms for token generation for short sequences (<= 256 tokens) under typical hardware profiles.
2. Limit peak bandwidth consumption for model refreshes to configurable budget (default 500 MB/hour per site).
3. Ensure safe upgrades: ability to rollback to last known-good artifact within 10 minutes (operator-mediated) or automatically revert on health regressions.
4. Preserve cryptographic provenance for all model artifacts and delta updates (signed manifests + detached signatures).

High-level architecture

Components:
- Central Deployment Orchestrator (control plane): produces signed manifest files describing model bundles, versioned artifacts, and delta patches. Runs in Redwood control plane or customer-managed private control plane.
- Delta Generator service: computes compact binary diffs between consecutive model artifact tarballs and emits patch packages. Integrates with model registry.
- Edge Sync Agent: lightweight process on the private deployment that pulls manifests, validates signatures, applies delta patches to local artifact store, and signals runtime to atomically swap model artifact directories.
- Local Serving Runtime: Redwood inference runtime configured for local artifact directories, KV cache preservation, and structured fallback to regional service when configured.
- Audit & Telemetry Gateway: batched telemetry shuttle and signed evidence collector that aggregates sync/upgrade events and ships evidence to the control plane when connectivity allows.

Architecture diagram (textual):
- Central Orchestrator --> publishes signed-manifest.json --> Edge Sync Agent
- Central Orchestrator --> Delta Generator --> delta-<vN>-<vN+1>.patch --> Edge Sync Agent
- Edge Sync Agent --(local apply)--> Local Artifact Store + runtime swap
- Local Serving Runtime --> Telemetry Gateway (batched) --> Central audit store

Key dataflows (numbered)

1. Manifest publish: Orchestrator composes manifest with metadata (model id, base artifact checksum, patch list, minimum-available-ram, hardware profile tag, rollout windows) and signs it using platform signing key.
2. Edge poll: Edge Sync Agent polls control plane for new manifests on configurable cadence (default: 30 minutes) or listens for push via an authenticated webhook when available.
3. Validation: Agent verifies manifest signature, checks local preconditions (disk free space, CPU/GPU idle threshold), and computes expected delta chain.
4. Fetch & apply: Agent downloads delta patches (or full artifact if delta chain broken), verifies detached signatures, applies patch into a new artifact directory, validates artifact (checksum + sample inference smoke test), then performs atomic symlink swap.
5. Evidence and telemetry: Agent records signed evidence of successful apply and local smoke-test output, pushes batched evidence when connectivity permits. If apply fails, the agent reverts to the previous artifact and raises an alert.

Manifest example (JSON snippet) - sample manifest should be treated as pseudocode when used in automation:

{
  "model_id": "redwood-2b-mix-quant",
  "version": "2026-02-05-3",
  "base_checksum": "sha256:abcdef...",
  "patches": ["delta-2026-01-27-to-2026-02-05.patch"],
  "min_free_disk_mb": 10240,
  "recommended_hw_tag": "t4-small|a10-large",
  "rollout_window": {"start_utc": "02:00","end_utc": "06:00"},
  "signature": "base64sig..."
}

Operational policies and rollout pattern

A. Canary phase (automated):
1. Publish manifest with rollout_window and target site list = small canary cohort (1–3 sites).
2. Edge Agents in cohort apply delta and run 10-minute smoke tests (API health, example prompts, model quality quick-check using curated seed prompts).
3. If telemetry indicates no CPU/GPU OOMs, P95 latency regressions, or quality regressions (see quality thresholds below) for 30 minutes, promote to progressive rollout.

B. Progressive rollout (time-based + health-gated):
1. Expand target cohort by percentage (10%, 25%, 50%, 100%) every rollout window cycle, monitor metrics for each expansion for a full window.
2. If any cohort emits critical failures (defined below), automatically pause rollout and notify oncall.

C. Emergency rollback:
- Edge Agent always keeps last known-good artifact locally. The agent can revert by atomic symlink back to previous artifact and restart runtime within 2 minutes. If automatic revert fails, operator-run rollback steps (see runbook) apply.

Quality and safety thresholds (monitored during rollout)

- Latency: P95 token latency increase <= 20% vs baseline.
- Error rate: 500-level error rate < 0.1% over 10 minute windows.
- Smoke-quality: Failure rate on curated prompts (semantic score) <= 3% relative degradation.

Upgrade and rollback procedure (detailed)

Pre-upgrade checks:
- Verify site has min_free_disk_mb from manifest + 20% buffer.
- Confirm no active high-priority operator tasks or live cutovers scheduled.
- Check telemetry shuttle backlog < 1000 events.
- Ensure operator has current artifact checksums and rollback artifact id.

Automated upgrade steps (agent-driven):
1. Agent receives signed manifest.
2. Agent validates and downloads delta(s).
3. Agent applies patch into new directory /var/lib/redwood/artifacts/<model>-<version>.<timestamp>.
4. Agent runs smoke tests (pass/fail). Smoke tests include: start inference daemon in isolated mode, run 5 seed prompts, validate output tokens and latency thresholds.
5. On success, Agent performs atomic swap and gracefully drains in-flight requests (config: drain_timeout = 30s).
6. Agent records signed apply-evidence and schedules telemetry upload.

Rollback (automated on health regression):
1. If post-swap health checks fail, Agent swaps back to previous artifact and restarts runtime.
2. Agent marks manifest as failed and attaches error_clues (failed smoke tests, checksum mismatch, insufficient disk).
3. Control plane creates incident with attached evidence bundle.

Manual rollback (operator):
1. SSH to operator bastion or use operator console.
2. Verify evidence bundle and determine root cause (failed patch, corrupted delta, quality regression).
3. Trigger remote rollback API: POST /operator/v1/sites/<site_id>/rollback with payload {"artifact_id": "..."}.
4. Validate site returns to previous SLOs and mark incident resolved.

Day-2 operations and runbook (troubleshooting checklist)

Common failure modes and recovery steps:
- Delta apply failure (checksum mismatch):
  1. Agent automatically attempts full artifact fetch.
  2. If full artifact fetch fails, agent halts and retains previous artifact, then raises CRITICAL alert to oncall.
- Disk pressure during apply:
  1. Agent aborts apply and cleans temporary files.
  2. Alert: "artifact.apply.disk_low". Operator must reclaim disk or expand ephemeral volume.
- Smoke-test degradation (semantic checks failing):
  1. Agent reverts immediately. 2. Oncall runs quality triage using sample inference traces, forwards artifacts to Applied ML for postmortem.
- Partial connectivity (patch download stalls):
  1. Agent resumes partial downloads with range requests and resumes after connectivity recovery; if unable within rollout_window, it aborts and schedules next attempt.

Runbook quick commands (agent-side):
- Force full artifact fetch: redwood-edge-agent fetch --site <id> --artifact <artifact_id> --force-full
- Query agent status: redwood-edge-agent status --site <id>
- Roll back to artifact: redwood-edge-agent rollback --artifact <artifact_id>

Hardware, network and customer requirements (table format described)

Table: Minimum site profile requirements
- CPU: 8 vCPU or equivalent (x86)
- RAM: 32 GB system RAM (64 GB recommended for model variants > 4B parameters)
- GPU: optional, recommended when model > 7B parameters. Supported tags in manifest must match actual installed GPU type.
- Disk: 25 GB free for runtime + model artifact working space (base artifact size + delta); ensure snapshot/backup partition available.
- Network: egress bandwidth >= 5 Mbps sustained for manifest sync windows; ability to make TLS connections to control-plane endpoints.

Customer operational commitments (minimum):
- Allowlist control-plane FQDNs in egress policy.
- Provide KMS/HSM integration info if customer-managed signatures required.
- Agree to rollout windows (local quiet hours) and provide operator contacts for emergency interventions.

Security and compliance considerations

- All manifests and artifacts must be signed with a platform-approved key; edge agent enforces signature verification.
- Evidence bundles contain minimal telemetry and MUST be redacted for PII by default before transit.
- For highly regulated customers, evidence bundles can be stored in-customer-premise and uploaded via an agreed transfer process.

Telemetry, logging and alerts

Critical metrics to emit from each site (batch/shuttle semantics):
- artifact.sync.success_rate (1m/5m windows)
- artifact.apply.duration.p95
- runtime.inference.p95_latency
- runtime.inference.error_rate
- disk.free_mb
- telemetry.upload.backlog_count

Critical alerts (examples):
- artifact.apply.failed (SEV2)
- runtime.inference.error_rate > 0.5% sustained (SEV1 for enterprise SLA customers)
- disk.free_mb < manifest.min_free_disk_mb + 1000MB (SEV2)

Acceptance tests and smoke checks (pre-flight)

- Deterministic smoke prompts: run canonical prompt set (5 prompts) verifying outputs match baseline signatures (semantic similarity > 0.92) and latencies within threshold.
- Artifact integrity: verify sha256 checksum and detached signature returned by control plane.
- End-to-end dry-run: simulate manifest application in staging agent and validate telemetry evidence creation.

Owners and escalation

- Secondary owner: eng-sre - edge-ops squad.
- Escalation path: oncall -> PD-ModelDist senior -> Edge-ops staff engineer -> Applied ML lead.

- retries = 8, backoff = exponential(base=5s, max=300s), use HTTP range requests, verify checksum after complete stream.
